children: Kuwait’s Public Authority for Housing Welfare (PAHW) plans to deliver about 4,750 homes across three residential developments being tendered under its real-estate developer partnership model, according to local Arabic language newspaper Al Anba.

Last month, the authority had prequalified 22 consortiums comprising 41 Kuwaiti and international companies for the projects in East Saad Al-Abdullah City (ESA-1); Al-Mutlaa (M-3), and West Saad Al Abdullah City and Jaber Al Ahmad (WSA-1 and J-1)

Al-Mutlaa City M3, the largest project tendered to date under the developer model, will provide around 2,500 homes across 2 million square metres (sqm). Six consortiums were prequalified from 16 applicants.
The 1 million sqm East Saad Al Abdullah City project is expected to provide around 1,250 homes. Eight consortiums were prequalified from 23 applicants.
West Saad Al Abdullah City and Jaber Al Ahmad (WSA-1 and J-1)

The third project, comprising a development in West Saad Al Abdullah City and a service hub in Jaber Al Ahmad City, is expected to provide around 1,000 homes. Eight consortiums were prequalified from 24 applicants.

PAHW is also preparing to develop larger residential cities, including Khiran City, Nawaf Al Ahmad City and Al-Sabriya City, the report said. The three cities are expected to address around 170,000 housing applications, while separate projects could provide an additional 10,000 housing units.
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)
